title: Karpenter CRDs still serve v1beta1, which 1.1 removes
quote: Karpenter `1.1.0` drops the support for `v1beta1` APIs. **Do not** upgrade to `1.1.0`+ without following the Migration Guide.
remediation: Complete the v1 migration on Karpenter 1.0 before upgrading past it. 1.0 serves v1beta1 through conversion webhooks; 1.1 drops that support, so any object still stored or served as v1beta1 stops being readable and the NodePools it describes provision nothing.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group | test("karpenter")) | "\(.metadata.name) served=\([.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | .name] | join(","))"'  # each Karpenter CRD and the API versions it still serves

title: Objects may still carry the v1beta1 compatibility annotations

detection.reason: the note does not name the annotation key, and inventing one would produce a rule that matches nothing while reading as clean — the compatibility annotations are written by the conversion webhook during the v1 migration

quote: Support for the `v1beta1` compatiblity annotations have been dropped. Ensure you have completed migration before upgrading to `v1.1.0`. Refer to the migration guide for more details.
remediation: Finish the v1 migration on 1.0 before upgrading. The compatibility annotations exist only to carry v1beta1 fields (notably the kubelet configuration) across the conversion, and 1.1 stops honouring them — anything still relying on one loses that configuration silently.
verifyCommand: kubectl get nodepools,nodeclaims -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[]? | .metadata.annotations // {} | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("karpenter")) | .key' | sort -u  # any compatibility.karpenter.sh annotation listed here is still carrying v1beta1 state

title: A NodePool or NodeClaim nodeClassRef is missing group or kind

detection.reason: reads the flag the agent writes whenever it could walk the object's nodeClassRef; an object whose spec could not be walked is reported as unchecked, never as clean

quote: `nodeClassRef.group` and `nodeClassRef.kind` are strictly required. Ensure these values are set for all `NodePools` / `NodeClaims` before upgrading.
remediation: Set `nodeClassRef.group` and `nodeClassRef.kind` on every NodePool and NodeClaim named here — for the AWS provider, group `karpenter.k8s.aws` and kind `EC2NodeClass`. Objects converted from v1beta1 carry only `nodeClassRef.name`, and from 1.1 those stop resolving their node class, so the NodePool provisions no capacity at all.
verifyCommand: kubectl get nodepools -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[]? | select((.spec.template.spec.nodeClassRef.group // "") == "" or (.spec.template.spec.nodeClassRef.kind // "") == "") | "NodePool/\(.metadata.name)"'; kubectl get nodeclaims -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[]? | select((.spec.nodeClassRef.group // "") == "" or (.spec.nodeClassRef.kind // "") == "") | "NodeClaim/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each object printed has an incomplete nodeClassRef and stops resolving its node class on 1.1

title: A Bottlerocket node class sets instanceStorePolicy RAID0
quote: Bottlerocket AMIFamily now supports `instanceStorePolicy: RAID0`. This means that Karpenter will auto-generate userData to RAID0 your instance store volumes (similar to AL2 and AL2023) when specifying this value.
remediation: Confirm the Bottlerocket image these node classes launch is v1.22.0 or later before upgrading. Karpenter starts auto-generating RAID0 userData for Bottlerocket, and on an older image the nodes fail to join the cluster — they come up and never register.

gate.reason: the RAID0 userData generation is specific to the Bottlerocket AMI family; on any other family the same instanceStorePolicy value is unaffected by this change

verifyCommand: kubectl get ec2nodeclasses -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[]? | select(.spec.amiFamily == "Bottlerocket" and .spec.instanceStorePolicy == "RAID0") | "\(.metadata.name) amiSelectorTerms=\((.spec.amiSelectorTerms // []) | tostring)"'  # each node class printed needs a Bottlerocket image of v1.22.0 or later

title: Pods select on the accelerator name that Neuron devices are losing

detection.reason: read from Pod rows as key=value pairs — nodeSelector is collected per pod, and node affinity is not scanned, so a clean result here does not clear an affinity term

quote: The AWS Neuron accelerator well known name label (`karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-accelerator-name`) values now reflect their correct names of `trainium`, `inferentia`, and `inferentia2`. Previously, all Neuron accelerators were assigned the label name of `inferentia`.
remediation: These pods pin `instance-accelerator-name=inferentia`. After the upgrade Trainium and Inferentia2 nodes report `trainium` and `inferentia2` instead of all reporting `inferentia`, so a selector written when they all shared one value now excludes them and the pods stop being scheduled onto that capacity.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods,deploy,statefulset,daemonset -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(tostring | test("instance-accelerator-name")) | "\(.kind)/\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each object printed pins an accelerator name whose value set changes on 1.1
